question: By which of the following authors was the English novel ‘Jude the Obscure’ written?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Thomas Hardy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Thomas Hardy** was an English novelist and poet who lived from 1840 to 1928.
 
• He is best known for his novels set in the semi-fictional region of Wessex, which corresponds to the south-west and south of England.
 
• **Jude the Obscure** was Hardy's last novel, published in 1895.
 
• The novel explores themes of class, education, religion, and marriage, reflecting Hardy's critical view of Victorian society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thomas Hardy's Literary Contributions:**

 
 
• Hardy wrote both novels and poetry, and he is considered one of the most significant English writers of the 19th century.
 
• Some of his other famous novels include "Tess of the d'Urbervilles," "Far from the Madding Crowd," and "The Mayor of Casterbridge."
 
• His works often focused on tragic characters struggling against their passions and social circumstances.
 
 
 
• **Victorian Literature:**
 
 
• Victorian literature refers to English literature during the reign of Queen Victoria (1837-1901).
 
• This period saw a flourishing of the novel as a literary form, with themes often addressing social issues, morality, and the consequences of the Industrial Revolution.
 
• Notable Victorian authors include Charles Dickens, the Brontë sisters, George Eliot, and Anthony Trollope.
 
 
 
• **Wessex:**
 
 
• Wessex is a fictional region created by Hardy, based on the real counties of Dorset, Somerset, Hampshire, and Wiltshire.
 
• Hardy's use of Wessex allowed him to create a detailed and consistent world in which his characters lived and interacted.
 
• The landscape and rural life of Wessex play a significant role in his storytelling, often reflecting the harsh realities of 19th-century rural England.
 
 
 
• **Themes in "Jude the Obscure":**
 
 
• The novel explores the struggles of Jude Fawley, a working-class young man who aspires to become a scholar.
 
• The themes include the rigidity of social class structures, the barriers to education, and the oppressive nature of marriage and religion.
 
• The book was controversial at the time of its publication for its critical portrayal of institutions and its depiction of sexual relationships.
